title: Splunk SOAR + ISE Closed-Loop Playbook Audit and Mean-Time-to-Containment KPI
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Splunk SOAR + ISE Closed-Loop Playbook Audit and Mean-Time-to-Containment KPI' only. Does not replace full NAC policy design or firewall rule authoring or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `network_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `network_splunk_soar_ise_closed_loop_playbook_audit_and_m` (UC-17.1.82), SOC dashboard panel "Network — Splunk SOAR + ISE Closed-Loop Playbook Audit and Mean-Time-to-Containment KPI", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:network_controls.

compliance.controlObjective: Mean-time-to-contain KPI for ANC-driven SOAR playbook executions.

compliance.assurance_rationale: DORA Art.17 ICT-related incident management — automated containment efficacy.
SOC-2 CC7.4 incident response — automated containment.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=phantom` sourcetype='cisco:ise:syslog' that satisfy the UC-17.1.82 SPL filters for 'Splunk SOAR + ISE Closed-Loop Playbook Audit and Mean-Time-to-Containment KPI'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `phantom` / `cisco:ise:syslog` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `network_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-17.1.82.

dataSources: Splunk SOAR audit logs `index=phantom` showing playbook runs, action results from the *Cisco ISE* SOAR app (https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4250) — `block_endpoint`, `unblock_endpoint`, `endpoint_session_info` actions. Combine with ISE syslog 86001 (ANC-applied) to audit reach.
app: `Splunk SOAR Cisco ISE App` (Splunkbase 4250) + Splunk SOAR.
spl:
index=phantom action_name=block_endpoint
| eval soar_apply_time=_time
| stats earliest(soar_apply_time) as soar_t, latest(_time) as last_action by container_id, mac_address
| join mac_address [search index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" MessageCode=86001 anc_action=quarantine | rename _time as ise_apply_time]
| eval soar_to_ise_lag_s=ise_apply_time - soar_t
| stats avg(soar_to_ise_lag_s) as avg_lag, max(soar_to_ise_lag_s) as max_lag
description: Audits Splunk SOAR playbook → ISE ANC closed-loop performance. Measures (a) SOAR `block_endpoint` action success rate, (b) average lag from SOAR action to ISE 86001 confirmation, and (c) max lag (worst case).
value: Automated containment is only as fast as its slowest link. SOAR playbook audit gives the SOC measurable evidence that playbooks executed end-to-end, satisfying NIS2/DORA incident-response requirements with quantitative MTTC.
implementation: Schedule the search every 1 hour over the last 24 hours; emit MTTC KPI to a summary index for the SOAR-effectiveness dashboard.
visualization: MTTC trend; per-playbook success rate; failed-action log.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Certificate or EAP profile rollout** — Clients fail EAP-TLS during staged cert deployment for 'Splunk SOAR + ISE Closed-Loop Playbook Audit and Mean-Time-to-Containment KPI'. Cross-check `FailureReason` and CMDB cert expiry.

2. **RADIUS/PSN maintenance restart** — Short auth failure burst while ISE node restarts. Match change window on `index=changes`.

3. **Guest or IoT onboarding surge** — Legitimate MAC registration spike skews `index=phantom` `cisco:ise:syslog` baselines.

4. **Approved pen-test or scanner traffic** — Red-team exercises from netblock in `approved_scanners.csv` mimic auth failures.

**Suppression mechanism:** `network_exception_register.csv` keyed on `CallingStationID`, `NAS-IP-Address`, `valid_until`.
mitreAttack: N/A (meta-detection — measures playbook execution KPIs, not adversary behaviour)
detailedImplementation:
Standard pattern.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk SOAR Cisco ISE App` (Splunkbase 4250) + Splunk SOAR.). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog into phantom, nac. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`container_id, mac_address`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Splunk SOAR is the automation that runs playbooks. When SOAR tells ISE to quarantine a device, we measure how long it takes — and prove the response actually happened.
